first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A planning service (Wedded Concierge) that will organise a wedding in Portugal for us, with a guide to regions, legal steps by passport and some cost info. The H1 'Get Married in Portugal, from a Sintra Palace to an Algarve Cliff' tells me the destination, not why these people and not the three other planners I have open. Two buttons, 'Find your region in Portugal' and 'Speak with a Wedded Advisor'. No price in the hero, which is fine, but also nothing that says they have actually done this before.

attention_map.quote: organised at least one month before the date
attention_map.why: A straight answer with an official source, not the 'six to twelve months' fluff every other tab says. Good. The brand line 'one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend' is the only reason to use them I can find up top, and it is a promise, not proof.

attention_map.quote: a non-numeric line naming Wedded Concierge and one Wedded Advisor, or hide the strip
attention_map.why: So at launch there is no number, no review, nothing. A 'proof strip' with no proof in it is just the company saying its own name again. If it is hidden I simply notice there is no proof anywhere near the top.

attention_map.quote: What can couples see and do in Portugal that no other country offers?
attention_map.why: Tourism-brochure stuff I can get anywhere. 'No other country offers' is the kind of big claim I discount. The Monserrate scaffolding note is the one line here that made me trust them a bit more.

attention_map.quote: Setting; Best months; Nearest airport (code); Guests
attention_map.why: Five cards with the same labels is great for comparing like for like, but 'Best months' is national only, so all five cards will say the same thing, and the Guests line is either gone or 'Ask your Wedded Advisor' on every card. Identical lines on five regions looks like filler and makes me check whether anything on the cards is region-specific at all.

attention_map.quote: events on those dates may have to be cancelled
attention_map.why: This is the catch, said out loud before I had to find it. State events can cancel a palace booking, nothing fixed to the heritage, Monserrate roof works to Q1 2027. Nobody else tells you this. Biggest trust moment in the whole page.

attention_map.quote: a permit from the local council or port authority
attention_map.why: Specific and sourced. Tells me there is a permit to budget for without pretending it is free.

attention_map.quote: Exclusivity can mean paying for unoccupied rooms; a buy-out is often separate from the venue fee
attention_map.why: Exactly the hidden costs I am hunting for. 'Check whether quotes include VAT' is useful. But it is all 'can', 'often', 'may' with no numbers, so I know what to ask about, not what it will cost.

attention_map.quote: Fallback until then: explain what drives cost (guest count, region, season, nights at the venue, exclusivity) with no figures, and offer a Wedded Advisor estimate.
attention_map.why: At launch the cost tab has no figures. 'Guest count, region, season' drives cost everywhere; that is not information. Even if the EUR 25,000 to 70,000 table appears later, it is someone else's average for 100 guests, not what this company charges or includes. Getting a number means getting on a call, which is the upsell funnel I am trying to avoid.

attention_map.quote: the US Embassy in Lisbon does not issue a CNI; you sign a statement of eligibility to marry before a consular officer
attention_map.why: Separate AU, US and UK routes, official sources, a 'checked October 2026' line. This is better than the planner blogs in my other tabs. The fee lines collapsing to 'a consular notarial fee applies' and 'the civil registry charges a fee' are small but they are exactly the kind of unanswered cost I notice.

attention_map.quote: Frame as what a weekend can include, planned by Wedded Concierge, not as a package inclusion list or price
attention_map.why: 'Can include' is the opposite of an inclusions list. No package, no price, no list of what is in and out. This is where I would expect to compare like for like with the competitors and I cannot.

attention_map.quote: hidden at launch: only 2 Portugal real weddings
attention_map.why: From the outside I just see no Portugal weddings at all. Two exist and are hidden. My question 'have you done this before?' gets nothing.

attention_map.quote: otherwise say a Wedded Advisor explains fees in your currency on the first call
attention_map.why: What does the service cost and what do I get for it? Answer: call us. That is the catch, right there. 'Why book through Wedded Concierge rather than the venue directly' is only promised 'from approved service facts', and I cannot see any approved fact in here beyond 'one Wedded Advisor'.

attention_map.quote: Ronaldo and Georgina's intimate Portugal wedding
attention_map.why: Four celebrity gossip links on a page where I am deciding on a planner, while their own real weddings are hidden. Feels like clickbait filling the space where proof should be.

attention_map.quote: Is a wedding in Portugal cheaper than at home?
attention_map.why: I would click this and get a non-answer, since there is no comparison and the Portugal range may not be signed off. A cost FAQ that cannot give a number reads as evasive.

questions_answered.question: What is NOT included in the from price?
questions_answered.evidence: There is no from price and no inclusions or exclusions list: 'No Wedded Wonderland figure and no From AUD price on this page', s6 is 'what a weekend can include', not a package. The venue charges box ('paying for unoccupied rooms', 'buy-out is often separate', check VAT) covers venue-side extras only, and fees are 'explained on the first call'.

questions_answered.question: Are these facts consistent across the page?
questions_answered.evidence: The brief clearly works at this: 'same wording in tabs, cards and FAQ', six months not three, one-month minimum everywhere, beach permit wording fixed. But the 'under 30' guest band in the qualifier has no matching cost band (only 'about 100 guests'), and five region cards with an identical national 'Best months' line will read as copy-paste rather than region facts.

questions_answered.question: What proof is there that this team has done this venue before?
questions_answered.evidence: B8 numbers 'UNCONFIRMED', fallback is a non-numeric line or hidden; real weddings 'hidden at launch'; founder quote and byline removed. No venue or region on the page is tied to a wedding they have run.

questions_answered.question: Why book through you and not the venue directly?
questions_answered.evidence: Only 'one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend' and the palace and venue-charges know-how by implication. The s10 answer is limited to 'approved service facts only' and none are given.

questions_answered.question: What happens if something goes wrong on the day?
questions_answered.evidence: Only 'an on-the-day coordinator' as something a weekend 'can include'. The brief itself lists 'what happens if something goes wrong on the day' as an open question with no approved line.

objections_triggered.objection: From price with no inclusions list means hidden costs
objections_triggered.triggered_by: No price at all, no inclusions list, and 'a Wedded Advisor explains fees in your currency on the first call'. Cost tab falls back to 'what drives cost' with no figures.
Proof strip empty or hidden, real weddings hidden, no reviews, no named venue they have worked with; only the company describing itself.

objections_triggered.objection: Inconsistent numbers (capacity or rooms differ in two places)
objections_triggered.triggered_by: Qualifier offers an 'under 30' band but costs exist only for 'about 100 guests'; region cards have a Guests label with nothing behind it. Not a contradiction yet, but gaps I would poke at.

objections_triggered.objection: Getting any number means a sales call
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'offer a Wedded Advisor estimate', 'explains fees ... on the first call', registry and consular fees reduced to 'a fee applies'.

trust_signals_noticed: Palace catch stated up front: 'events on those dates may have to be cancelled' and Monserrate scaffolding to Q1 2027
Venue charges box naming unoccupied rooms, buy-outs, per-guest minimums and VAT
Legal steps split by AU, US and UK passport with official sources linked
'Legal and cost details checked October 2026, with sources named in each tab.'
Honest 'no package, a planned weekend instead' rather than a fake package
No superlatives in the H1, no urgency tactics, no venue capacities lifted from other sites
turn_offs_noticed: 'that no other country offers' (superlative claim in the spotlight)
Celebrity trending row (Ronaldo, Perrie Edwards) standing in where real weddings should be
'Fall for Portugal Before You Choose a Venue' and 'Celebrate More Than a Wedding' read as padding
Repeated 'Speak with a Wedded Advisor' as the answer to every cost and service question

emotional_response.overall: Respect for the honesty about the catches at the venues, irritation that the same honesty is not applied to their own service. They tell me exactly what a palace or a quinta might sting me for, then go quiet on what they charge and what they have done.
emotional_response.strongest_negative: s10-advisor fee line and hidden real weddings

payload.decision_reason: I would use this page as a reference for the legal rules and venue catches, but not to pick a planner. I am deciding this week and two of my questions get nothing at all: no proof they have run a single wedding in Portugal (the proof strip is empty and the real weddings are hidden), and no idea what the service costs or includes beyond 'a Wedded Advisor explains fees on the first call'. The other tabs I have open at least show me their weddings. My rule is no enquiry while a cost question or the proof question is still open, and both are open here.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Honestly, this is the most upfront page I have seen about what a Portugal venue might sting you for, the palace cancellations, the unoccupied rooms, the VAT. Then I get to their bit and it is 'speak with a Wedded Advisor' for the fee and nothing to show they have ever done a wedding here. Two real weddings and they hid them, but there are four Ronaldo links. What's the catch? Probably the catch is on the first call. I'll grab the legal checklist and go with someone who shows me their work.
